Header: Amsacta albistriga Sivappu Kambali Puzhu / சிவப்புகம்பளிபுழு

Prevention: Destroy the pupae through summer ploughing.
Collect volunteer plants from harvested field and destroy by burning.
Dig a trench around the field at 30 cm depth and 25 cm width to arrest the movement of migrating larvae.
Raise one row of cowpea (Thatta payir) for every 5 rows of groundnut wherever red hairy caterpillar is endemic (predominant at a particular place).
T-shaped bird perches (10 to 15/ac) to encourage predators.
Monitoring: Setup 1 light trap/acre from planting and observe regularly between 6- 9 pm.
Install sex pheromone trap (Amsactin lure) at 5/ac from planting, when 2-3 eggs are found for every 10 plants.
Observe for faecal matter and defoliation symptoms at 6-8 am twice a week.
This pest affects the vegetative stage.
It causes defoliation, where all the leaves are eaten, leaving the main stem alone.
Larvae are reddish brown with black bands on both ends and long reddish brown hairs all over the body.
Adult moths have white forewings with brownish streaks all over and a yellowish streak along the anterior margin and head.
Hind wings are white with black markings.
Direct Control: Spray in the evening hours with a hand sprayer.
NSKE in 500 litres of water for 8 hours, filter and add 500 ml of teepol to spray 1
Neem oil at 30 ml in 1 litre of water at 15 day intervals.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, pre- harvest interval, max number of sprays, restricted re-entry interval.
Do not empty into drains and water sources.
Phosalone 35EC at 2ml/litre of water at 15-20 day intervals.
Chlorpyriphos at 2 ml/litre water at 15-20 day intervals.
